name: Women's Society of Cyberjutsu
summary: Women's Society of Cyberjutsu (WSC) is a nonprofit dedicated to advancing women in cybersecurity through free training, mentorship, scholarships, and networking. Their Slack connects members for career advice, study groups, and local chapter meetups, and is explicitly built to welcome newcomers regardless of experience level. It suits women (and allies) at any stage, from those exploring the field to working professionals.
rules_note: Join via the free signup page linked from womenscyberjutsu.org; some WSC programs (training, scholarships) require separate membership registration.

name: WICCA
summary: Run by a Netherlands-based nonprofit for women in cybersecurity, this Discord connects members for networking, events, and a newsletter tied to the group's broader mission of inspiring and supporting women in the field. It suits women (students through professionals) looking for community, events, and career connections rather than deep technical training.
rules_note: Open Discord invite link; broader org also runs in-person events and a newsletter.

name: Haecksen (CCC)
summary: Haecksen is a feminist hacker and tech collective loosely associated with the Chaos Computer Club scene, where members network nationwide around digital self-defense, net politics, data protection, and general hacking/activism. It suits women and gender-marginalized people in tech who want a community-run space, though joining the chat requires emailing an admin for an SSO account rather than a self-service link.
rules_note: Not a self-service invite: email admin@haecksen.org with a desired nickname to request an SSO account for rocket.haecksen.org; a mailing list join is also expected.
candidate_notes: Affinity: women, lgbtq; org: Haecksen; join: request-form; scope: security. Primary chat is RocketChat, not Discord/Slack/Matrix. Requires requesting SSO credentials from admin@haecksen.org and joining their mailing list first — not a pure self-service invite link.

name: InfosecGirls
summary: InfosecGirls is a community-run group (India-based, with chapters) for women and students curious about information security, organizing monthly meetups, webinars, and mentoring alongside a job-resources page. It's aimed squarely at newcomers exploring infosec as a career, joined through a public Google Group forum.
rules_note: Join via free signup on the public Google Group forum linked from the site's Join Us page.
candidate_notes: Affinity: women; org: InfosecGirls; join: free-signup; scope: security. Community for women/students in infosec, founded 2014. Uses a Google Group as its public forum; no Discord/Slack found on official site.

summary: Raíces Cyber is a nonprofit built to help Hispanic, Latino, and Latinx people break into and grow in cybersecurity careers, and this Discord is described as the community's home base for networking, mentorship, and support. It's welcoming to beginners and students entering the field, not just working professionals.
discord_description: We empower people to forge cybersecurity careers and help build a more inclusive generation of cyber defenders.
candidate_notes: Affinity: other; org: Raíces Cyber Org; join: open-link; scope: security. name: ColorStack

It's a general CS/tech career community rather than security-specific, but it maintains a dedicated career-cybersecurity channel for members interested in the field. Best suited for students who want broader tech community and mentorship with a side channel for security career questions.
rules_note: Membership/signup required via colorstack.org (student verification typically expected); Slack invite is a share-link, not a public self-serve page.

name: Cyversity

It's a paid membership community platform ($100/year professionals, $20/year students and veterans) rather than a free chat space, suited to people seeking structured career support.
rules_note: Requires paid membership ($100/year professional, $20/year student or veteran) via the signup portal, not a free chat space.

It's a membership application portal rather than a chat community, geared toward structured career and leadership development.

It suits LGBTQ+ people and allies working in or around technology who want peer support and networking, rather than someone looking for a dedicated security learning space.

name: VeteranSec
summary: VeteranSec is a nonprofit Slack community for current and former military members from any country working in or entering cybersecurity, run by a small group of volunteer admins. Members discuss exploit development, reverse engineering, CTF writeups, penetration testing, wireless hacking, and certification and career guidance, and it doubles as a networking and mentorship space for veterans in the field.
rules_note: Join by submitting an application form (name/handle, email, military branch, LinkedIn, background); membership restricted to current or former military personnel working in cybersecurity.
candidate_notes: Affinity: veterans; org: VeteranSec; join: request-form; scope: security. Small private Slack of cybersecurity veterans at all career stages; you must fill out a contact form (name, email, military branch, LinkedIn, background) and they send a Slack invite. Open to current/former military of any country working in cybersecurity. Distinct organization from VetSec (vetsec.org) despite the similar name.

name: Operation Code
summary: Operation Code is a nonprofit serving military veterans, active-duty service members, and military spouses who are learning to code and building tech careers, offering mentorship, scholarships, and a Slack community. It's a general software-development and tech-career community rather than security-focused, though some members pursue cybersecurity tracks and can find peers there. Best suited for veterans/military-affiliated people early in a tech career transition.

candidate_notes: Affinity: veterans; org: Operation Code; join: free-signup; scope: tech-with-security-channel. General software-dev/tech-career focus rather than security-specific, though members include those on security tracks; free signup with email/name/zip grants a Slack invite.
